This video makes a hash of the explanation.

The answer is, PC-DOS/MS-DOS was an imitator of CPM/86, which was a variant of CP/M, and used many of the same conventions. CP/M was released in 1974, years before the IBM PC, and had to deal with serious space limitations.

When the IBM PC came out, the default amount of memory was 16K. Not 16Gb or even 16Mb. 16384 individual bytes for the interrupt table, kernel, BIOS data area and on top of all that, whatever program you wanted to run. Still not enough room to waste with big fancy filenames.
